chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from 'Ubay ibn Hisham from Aban ibn 'Uthman from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdullah from Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A man was captured by the Romans and did not fast the month of Ramadan, and he does not know which month it is.' He said, 'He should fast a month that he anticipates and intends for it; if the month he fasted was before Ramadan, it will not suffice him, and if it was after the month of Ramadan, it will suffice him.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: It sufficed him (as a valid makeup)
key_terms.الرُّومُ: The Romans (Byzantines), referring to the captors in this context
key_terms.لَمْ يُجْزِهِ: It does not suffice him (as a valid makeup)
key_terms.يَحْتَسِبُ بِهِ: He intends/counts it (as a religious deed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who missed Ramadan fasting due to captivity and is unsure of the current month?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the flexibility in *qada'* (makeup fasting) when specific temporal markers are unknown due to captivity. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the obligatory month of Ramadan and the general act of fasting, ensuring the captive is not penalized for uncertainty while maintaining the integrity of the religious obligation.
